title: Pexels chrome pass: ambient imagery and credits
spec: Use the Pexels key to dress the surfaces T-5 built: shelf/kind headers, the empty state, the backdrop behind the carousel, the Seen archive header. AMBIENT IMAGERY ONLY — Pexels is never a source of title artwork; stock photos cannot supply key art and a poster wall made of them is the spreadsheet problem in costume. Follow GLP-Strong-App's pattern: a fetch script that runs ONCE and saves files into the frontend's public tree, plus a credits.json recording creator, license, source URL, photographer URL, alt text and why each image was chosen. These images ARE committed (they are generic and a fresh clone should look right) — unlike title art, which stays in gitignored data/. Images must work under every skin, so they sit behind token-driven scrims rather than dictating colour. ACCEPT: every shipped image has a credits.json row with real attribution; no surface depends on a network call at runtime.

plan.evidence: PLAN: (1) scripts/fetch-chrome.py — searches Pexels once per slot, downloads to frontend/public/chrome/, writes credits.json; (2) CSS hooks so each dressed surface reads a background from a token-driven class with a scrim over it; (3) run it, commit the images and credits; (4) re-run the regression greps and the traversal check. DECISIONS: the script is idempotent and skips a slot whose file already exists, so re-running it does not re-spend API quota or churn the committed files; images are downsized-by-request via Pexels' own sized URLs rather than shipping originals; and every image is applied UNDER a token scrim so a skin decides the mood and the photograph only supplies texture.

auto-review.evidence: REVIEWED — one defect, found and fixed, and worth recording as a lesson. I introduced --ink-over-art for text over photographs and USED it without DEFINING it: the insertion anchor in :root no longer matched because T-8 had edited that region. CSS does not complain about an undefined custom property — var() falls back silently — so the archive banner heading rendered in --ink, near-black rgb(26,24,21), over a dark photograph. It was caught only because the test asserted the COMPUTED colour rather than checking the stylesheet contained the right text. After the fix all three skins report rgb(255,255,255) and the title-page hero, which shares the token, does too. The lesson recorded for any future styling work: an undefined CSS custom property fails silently and looks like a deliberate choice, so assert computed values rather than source text. The token itself is justified rather than an exception to the no-literals rule: text over a photograph cannot use --ink because in a light skin that is near-black and unreadable over a dark still, but a bare #fff would have broken the rule every other ticket kept — a token fixes the value to the medium while leaving a skin able to override it.

uat.evidence: ACCEPT cleared under GA-1. VISION-CONFORMANCE against T-1: the games amendment and the data-source rules both state that Pexels is for chrome and never for title artwork, and this ticket holds that line — the three images are a texture, an auditorium and a shelf, none of them pretending to be cover art. T-1's objective that the app be pleasant rather than merely correct is what this ticket serves, and it does so without touching the privacy boundary: these images are committed BECAUSE they are generic, while every cached poster stays gitignored. Against non-goals: nothing added here touches episode tracking, sharing, recommendations or the bind address.
